propositions: Cross-subtree link escalation substitutes the requested edge for different endpoints without returning the substitution record to library and MCP callers, only to CLI via stdout.

The redirect record is emitted to stdout only, then discarded by quiet sinks in three propagation layers (_link closure, _python_leaf return, rebar.link return), leaving MCP and library callers unaware that a substitution occurred.
Removing quiet would corrupt the MCP JSON-RPC stream, so the record must be returned as a value instead of relying on stdout as the sole channel.
The five-layer propagation chain (add_dependency → link_core → _link → _python_leaf → rebar.link) must thread the redirect record through return values, with three layers currently dropping it.
link_tickets must report the resolved endpoints in its return string when escalation occurs, changing from 'ok' to 'ok (escalated: source->target recorded as resolved_source->resolved_target)'.
